calls.head: Power vs. Power
calls.body: At home, the Flames keep sending Coronato’s line (Farabee, Backlund and Coronato) out against opponents’ first lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Ryan Huska has been choosing strength on strength. Tonight the Rangers’ first line is Lafrenière, Zibanejad and Perreault.

calls.happened: Calgary’s L1 (Farabee, Backlund, Coronato) spent 46% of its 5-on-5 time against the Rangers’ L1 (5:36 of 12:14). The call needed 53%, halfway from the 39% it would get with no line matching to its home habit of 67%.

calls.head: The Rangers hunt better looks than the Flames
calls.body: On shot quality, the Rangers are one of the league’s best, but Calgary is the worst. They’re about as far apart as two teams get. The more dangerous chances should be the Rangers’.
calls.call: The Rangers’ shots are more dangerous on average than the Flames’.

surprises.head: Both teams played to type
surprises.body: Nothing in this game strayed far from how these two usually play: the shot share, the quality of chances, special teams, hitting, ice time and goaltending all landed inside their normal night-to-night range.

story.head: Zibanejad has two goals as the Rangers beat the Flames
paras: Mika Zibanejad struck first for the Rangers just 59 seconds into the second. He struck again on the power play midway through the period to make it 2-0, and that one stood up as the winner. Adam Klapka cut the Rangers’ lead to 2-1 on the power play early in the third, and Tye Kartye shut the door with an empty-netter with just seven seconds left.

The chances were close to even, so this one could have gone either way. Joonas Korpisalo, in his second game since coming over from Boston, made 29 saves for the Rangers, and Devin Cooley stopped 21 of 23 at the other end. The Rangers improved to 11-8-1, third in the Metropolitan, while the Flames fell to 8-10-1, slipping to sixth in the Pacific.
